comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C1-C6. Both OpenEval and peer reviewers support the foundational experimental system, RIAIL generation, and observation of genetic variation in spindle traits. Peer reviewers praised this as a 'tour de force' imaging effort.

Disagreement on claims C7-C8 (Timer model rejection). OpenEval finds the correlation analysis and statistical reasoning sound, while peer reviewers requested clarification on 'the link between partial correlations and correlations,' finding it 'not obvious' and creating uncertainty about the conclusions.

Disagreement on claims C9-C12 (Limiting Component model rejection via partial correlation). OpenEval supports the statistical approach as appropriate, while peer reviewers found the statistical reasoning insufficiently explained, requesting clarification on the relationship between partial and simple correlations.

Disagreement on claims C13-C16 (cell length importance and Boundary model rejection). OpenEval finds the statistical evidence strong and logic clear, while peer reviewers questioned the clarity of the correlation analysis interpretation, creating uncertainty about the strength of conclusions.

Disagreement on claims C17-C23 (QTL mapping results). OpenEval supports the statistical approach and conditional analysis as sound, while peer reviewers viewed these findings as confirmatory rather than novel, questioning whether the QTL analysis added significant new understanding beyond existing knowledge of gpr-1/2 and par-2.

Disagreement on claims C24-C30 (candidate gene identification and validation). OpenEval finds convergent evidence from genetic mapping and RNAi validation strong, while peer reviewers noted that gpr-1/2 and par-2 roles were demonstrated years ago, questioning the novelty of these findings.

Disagreement on claims C31-C33 (laser ablation demonstrating pulling forces). OpenEval finds the experimental design appropriate and inference sound, while peer reviewers raised concerns about 'intrinsic caveats,' missing controls (genetic evidence, immunofluorescent staining), and noted all experiments were on posterior half only.

Disagreement on claims C34-C39 (minimal spindle force contribution). OpenEval supports the convergent evidence from laser ablation and genetic perturbation, while peer reviewers identified a 'clear discrepancy' with Garzon-Coral et al., 2016 (which found pushing forces during anaphase) and noted missing controls.

Disagreement on claims C40-C43 (multidirectional pulling forces). OpenEval finds the perpendicular ablation results provide strong evidence for force balance, while peer reviewers noted all ablation experiments were performed on posterior half and requested anterior controls, creating uncertainty about generalizability.

Disagreement on claims C44-C49 (Stoichiometric Model description and stability). OpenEval finds the computational evidence strong, while peer reviewers stated authors 'did not do a good job in explaining the mechanism' and noted the catastrophe rate (0.025/s) 'seems extremely low' compared to literature values (1-10/s in Kozlowski et al.).

Disagreement on claims C50-C53 (stoichiometry necessity for stability). OpenEval supports the comparative simulation evidence, while peer reviewers urged authors 'to explain the mechanism of stabilizing the central centrosome position and not just to state that their mechanism does so,' indicating insufficient mechanistic explanation.

Disagreement on claims C54-C57 (single centrosome ablation validation). OpenEval finds strong agreement between simulation and experiment, while peer reviewers noted a critical discrepancy with Krueger et al., 2010 where single centrosome (via zyg-1 RNAi) came to rest at 60% egg length, not center, creating uncertainty about interpretation.

Disagreement on claims C58-C61 (asymmetric positioning explanation). OpenEval supports the model's ability to reproduce experimental dynamics, while peer reviewers noted 'the role of LET-99 is completely ignored' and that LET-99 inhibits lateral posterior pulling forces (Krueger et al., 2010), inconsistent with the model's uniform posterior force assumption.

Disagreement on claims C62-C67 (quantitative model-data agreement). OpenEval finds strong statistical validation across datasets, while peer reviewers questioned whether the model 'represents a significant advance' over Bouvrais et al., 2018 and noted the omission of LET-99 creates uncertainty about capturing full biological complexity.

Partial overlap on claims C68-C75 (model synthesis). OpenEval supports the model's mechanistic grounding (C70-C72), while peer reviewers questioned the mechanistic explanation and parameter choices, particularly the catastrophe rate and lack of detail about stochastic simulation implementation.

Partial overlap on claims C68-C75 (model synthesis). OpenEval supports the model's explanatory power (C73-C74), while peer reviewers acknowledged the model 'explains the dynamics and variability' but questioned whether it advances beyond prior models and noted the LET-99 omission.

Partial overlap on claim C69 (laser ablation integration). OpenEval supports the integration of laser ablation with modeling, while peer reviewers raised substantial concerns about laser ablation methodology, missing controls, and discrepancies with prior work.

Partial overlap on claim C79 (evolutionary consistency). OpenEval supports the consistency of correlations across evolutionary scales, while peer reviewers' concerns about the model's biological completeness (LET-99 omission) create uncertainty about the evolutionary interpretation.

OpenEval evaluated claims C80-C84 (background on C. elegans cell division) as supported by foundational literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as these are established background claims.

OpenEval evaluated claims C85-C87 (scaling phenomenon context and knowledge gap) as supported by extensive citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as these establish context rather than novel findings.

Disagreement on claim C88 (model's comprehensive explanatory power). OpenEval supports this as a summary of validated results, while peer reviewers questioned whether the model represents a significant advance and noted the LET-99 omission limits its comprehensiveness.
